title: Company-wide policies and processes
author: Monica Patel
body:
Overview

Purpose
This document centralizes Redwood Inference’s company-wide policies and standard operating procedures for access & permissions, change management, data management, procurement & expenses, vendor management, travel, and internal templates. The goal is to provide a single, maintainable reference for employees, managers, and approvers.

Scope
Applies to all Redwood employees, contractors, vendors with network/console access, and any third parties that process Redwood data. Exceptions must be approved by the policy owner (People Ops) and recorded in the related_pages list with justification.

Owners and review cadence
- Policy owner: People Ops (policy-level questions)
- Technical owner (access & change processes): Eng Infra
- Security owner (data and vendor controls): Security & Compliance
- Review cadence: Annual (next review scheduled 2027-03-01)

1) Access & permissions
Principles
- Principle of least privilege: grant only the minimum permissions required for a role or task.
- Role-based access: use groups and roles (SSO/Groups) rather than individual privileges where possible.
- Just-in-time and short-lived credentials encouraged for sensitive actions.

Identity and authentication
- Single sign-on (SSO) through Okta is the canonical identity provider.
- MFA required for all staff accounts (hardware token or authenticator app).
- Service accounts must be pinned to machine/service identity and documented in the service registry.

Onboarding & offboarding (checklist)
1. New hire request submitted in HRIS triggers Access Request form (see Templates).
2. Manager selects role template; system auto-assigns default groups for role.
3. Security and IRSA review for roles that access PII/regulated data.
4. Confirm MFA enrollment and sign required policies (Acceptable Use, Data Handling).
5. Offboarding: deactivate Okta account within 4 hours of termination for high privilege roles, 24 hours standard.

Access request and approval flow
- Standard access: submit request via Access Request template; manager approval within 3 business days.
- Elevated/privileged access (e.g., prod DB write, root cluster access): manager + security approval required; access reviewed weekly and granted for a maximum of 8 hours unless extended with justification.
- Emergency access: follow the Emergency Access Procedure in the Security docs (must be logged and reviewed).

Periodic access review
- Quarterly automated group membership snapshot and manager attestation.
- Annual privileged access audit by Security with remediation plan recorded.

2) Change management
Change categories
- Standard change: low-risk, repeatable (e.g., configuration tweaks). Pre-approved and executed during standard business hours.
- Minor change: moderate risk (e.g., non-breaking infra updates). Change request (RFC) required; scheduled within maintenance windows.
- Major change: high risk (schema migrations, major infra topology changes). CAB review required. Rollout plan, test matrix, and rollback plan mandatory.
- Emergency change: outage mitigation; post-facto CAB review required within 3 business days.

Change schedule and windows
- Regular maintenance windows: Sat 03:00–07:00 UTC (low traffic). Any major change outside these windows needs CAB approval.

RFC / Change request requirements (minimum)
- Title, owner, target systems/services, staging plan, test plan, rollback steps, monitoring and validation checklist, expected impact, blackout periods.
- Example: RFC-2026-ENG-1838 (use RFC template in Templates).

Approval SLAs and CAB
- Minor changes: manager + service owner approval within 48 hours.
- Major changes: present to CAB (weekly meeting). Decision recorded and linked in related_pages.
- CAB membership: Engineering leaders, SRE, Security, Product representative for impacted product.

Deployment checklist (example)
1. Pre-deploy runbook verified and published.
2. Automated tests and integration tests pass in staging.
3. Backups and snapshots taken (if applicable).
4. Monitoring dashboards and alerts configured for post-deploy validation.
5. Stakeholder notification completed 24 hours before change.

Rollback and postmortem
- Rollback plan must be executable with a maximum RTO of defined service SLO.
- All production-impacting failed changes must produce a postmortem within 5 business days and remediation tracked in the action tracker.

3) Data management
Data classification
- Public: information intended for public disclosure.
- Internal: company-internal, non-sensitive.
- Confidential: PII, business-sensitive data.
- Regulated: customer data subject to contractual/regulatory controls (e.g., PCI, HIPAA).

Handling rules (by classification)
- Public: no restrictions.
- Internal: store in internal wiki/services, not indexed by external search.
- Confidential/Regulated: encrypt at rest and in transit, limit access by role, log all access, do not copy to onboarding sandboxes.

Storage, retention and deletion
- Canonical storage: S3 buckets with server-side encryption (AES-256) for object storage; production DBs use KMS-managed keys.
- Retention: default data retention is 3 years unless regulatory or contractual obligations dictate otherwise.
- Deletion: follow Data Deletion Request template; deletions must be logged and verified by Data Steward.

Backups and disaster recovery
- Nightly backups for production DBs with point-in-time recovery for 7 days.
- Full backup retention: 90 days; incremental snapshots retained per infra runbook.

Data access review
- Quarterly automated access reports for all confidential/regulatory datasets, manager attestation, and security verification.

Logging and monitoring
- All access to regulated data must be auditable: include user, timestamp, object, action, source IP.
- Logs retained per compliance policy: 13 months for standard logs, 7 years for security-sensitive logs when required by customer contract.

4) Procurement and expenses
Procurement thresholds and approvals (matrix)
- <= $1,000: Manager approval.
- $1,001–$25,000: Manager + Finance approval.
- $25,001–$250,000: Director + Finance + Legal review.
- > $250,000: VP-level approval, Legal and Finance sign-off, and procurement lead involvement.

Purchase order (PO) and vendor setup
- All purchases that require a PO must go through Finance’s procurement system.
- New vendor onboarding requires completed Vendor Risk Assessment (see Vendor Management section).

Corporate cards and expense policy
- Corporate card issuance requires manager nomination and Finance approval.
- Personal expense reimbursement: submit receipts and Expense Report within 30 days. Finance processes reimbursements within 10 business days of submission.
- Forbidden expenses: personal entertainment not related to business, cash advances without approval, expenses violating travel limits.

Travel booking & per diem (summary)
- Book travel through the approved travel provider. Economy class for flights <8 hours, Premium Economy or Business with Director approval for longer flights.
- Per diem rates align with GSA regions for domestic travel and local guidance for international travel.

Expense audit and recovery
- Finance reserves the right to audit expense reports and request additional documentation up to 6 months after submission. Policy violations may require repayment or disciplinary action.

5) Vendor management
Vendor risk categories
- Low: SaaS tools with no customer data access (e.g., payroll reporting).
- Medium: vendors that process internal or aggregated logs without PII.
- High: vendors with access to customer data, production systems, or sensitive IP.

Onboarding checklist
1. Complete vendor intake form (Templates).
2. Vendor Risk Assessment (security questionnaire).
3. Contract review by Legal (SLA, data residency, termination, breach notification).
4. Security evidence (ISO/SOC, penetration test reports) collected for Medium/High risk.
5. Vendor access scoped and provisioned through a time-limited IAM account; review cadence set.

Contract lifecycle management
- Contracts stored in the Contracts registry (Legal). Renewal reminders at 90/60/30 days before expiry.
- SLAs and escalation points must be included for production-facing vendors.

Vendor offboarding
- Revoke all vendor accounts, terminate active sessions, remove network/VPN access, collect final deliverables and confirm data deletion per contract.
- Record offboarding checklist completion in the vendor record.

6) Travel policies (detailed)
Pre-approval
- All business travel requires manager pre-approval in the travel system. International travel requires Security notification for higher-risk locations.

Booking rules
- Use preferred travel vendor; exceptions require manager justification and Finance pre-approval.
- Employees must book refundable fares when travel dates are uncertain and use the lowest reasonable fare consistent with policies.

Health & safety
- Employees traveling internationally should register travel with People Ops and complete any required vaccinations or travel insurance.
- Emergency contact procedures and insurance policy numbers must be documented on the Travel Request form.

Expense limits (examples)
- Meals: up to $75/day (domestic); up to $120/day (high-cost cities) with receipts.
- Ground transport: rideshare or economy car rental; prefer public transit when safe and practical.

7) Internal templates (where to find and how to use)
Available templates (link and short description)
- Access Request template — use to request role or elevated permissions (Auto-created from HRIS triggers).
- Change Request (RFC) template — includes fields for rollout plan, rollback, validation metrics.
- Purchase Request / PO template — fill for any purchase requiring a PO.
- Vendor Intake & Risk Assessment — questionnaire for new vendors.
- Data Deletion Request — formal request to remove data from canonical stores.

RFC (Change Request) skeleton (example)\- Title: "[Service] - Short description - YYYYMMDD"
- Owner: name + pager/team
- Target: services/environments
- Pre-deploy checks: list
- Rollback steps: list
- Post-deploy validation: queries/dashboards/alert checks

Access Request example (CLI snippet for automation)
- Submit via CLI (internal tool):
  redwood-access create --user user@example.com --role data-analyst --reason \"Onboarding: analytics team\" --expires 2026-04-01

Enforcement and exceptions
- Non-compliance with policies will be handled by People Ops and Security depending on the policy domain. Exceptions must be documented and approved by the policy owner and Security when applicable.

Appendix: contacts and escalation
- People Ops (policy owner): people-ops@redwood.example.com
- Security (data & vendor controls): security@redwood.example.com
- Finance (procurement/expense): finance@redwood.example.com
- Eng Infra (change & access tooling): eng-infra@redwood.example.com

Revision history

- 2026-03-04: Published, reviewers Jake Morris, Aisha Khan, Tom Becker updated approval matrix and templates links.
